newsitem.title: USA: Downward pressure on U.S. cheese prices seen.
newsitem.headline: Downward pressure on U.S. cheese prices seen.

text.p: Large inventories should push U.S. cheese prices lower in coming weeks ahead of the start-up of a new cash cheese market at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, the Dairy and Food Market Analyst newsletter said.

Privately held stocks of cheese totalled 380.4 million lbs at the end of February, up 36 million lbs from a year earlier, according to the U.S. Agriculture Department's monthly Cold Storage report on Friday.

"Buyers are beginning to back away from the market," the newsletter said in its weekly bulletin. "Demand for barrels is considerably weaker than demand for natural cheese. And cheese is still moving out of the West, weakening prices further.
"Under this environment, we expect the block price to start to decline within the next few weeks unless traders wait for the new CME cash cheese market to open May 2," it said.

The CME said on March 20 that cheese industry leaders agreed to transfer the trading on the National Cheese Exchange (NCE) in Green Bay, Wisconsin, to the new market proposed by the CME. The NCE had been criticized by dairy farmers and Wisconsin state officials as a closed market dominated by a few dairy industry processing giants.
NCE will conduct its last weekly trading session on April 25. The new CME market will trade blocks and barrels of cheddar and also at the outset trade in one session a week.
As a CME market, operations will be subject to scrutiny by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
"The main difference is that trading will be anonymous through brokers," the newsletter said. "We believe this featrure will facilitate greater participation from traders."
At the NCE on Friday, barrels were quoted at $1.2550 a lb and blocks at $1.3250. The price of AA butter at the Chicago Butter Exchange was $1.1600 a lb.
